metadata.description: Seb's AI tools: Claude Code skills and agents, one plugin each.

plugins.name: write-clear-explainers
plugins.description: Write and review technical explainers for readers who are technical but new to the system.

plugins.name: test-gnosis-vpn
plugins.description: Install, fund and test the latest Gnosis VPN client on a remote Linux server over SSH without locking yourself out, from a throwaway VM to returning its funds.

plugins.name: report-gnosis-vpn-results
plugins.description: Report, summarize and compare Gnosis VPN test results from gnosis_vpn-bench runs in a standard way, and push them to a private results repository as soon as a run produces them.

plugins.name: commit-reviewer
plugins.description: Independent read-only reviewer agent: give it a commit range and it answers APPROVED or NOT APPROVED with findings, after reading the repository's AI guide and running its tests.

plugins.name: review-loop
plugins.description: Send the latest local commits to the reviewer session running next to this one, fix its findings, resubmit, and push only on APPROVED.

plugins.name: review-swarm
plugins.description: Run a review swarm that coordinates through a shared work board: reviewers audit one area each, short-lived validators judge their findings, devs fix them in parallel with their own commit-reviewers, and a test-gated merge queue merges each fix, watched on a terminal and a web dashboard.

plugins.name: reflect
plugins.description: Retrospective over agent sessions, including long multi-agent runs: scores friction deterministically across a session and its subagents, then proposes most-severe-first fixes to the environment, skills and workflows. Proposes only.

author.name: Teebor-Choka, extended by Sebastian C. Bürgel

plugins.name: reboot-resume
plugins.description: Persist the Claude Code sessions running on a Linux machine, interactive and background, and reopen them after a restart, one terminal tab each, in the right folder with the same flags.

plugins.name: safe-bash
plugins.description: A hook that refuses Bash commands matching processes by their full command line (pkill -f, pgrep -f), which also match, and kill, the shell running them.
